newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Russian news takes shine off De Beers shares.
newsitem.headline: Russian news takes shine off De Beers shares.

text.p: Shares in De Beers sank on Wednesday on concerns about future relations with Russia, despite news of record rough diamond sales in 1996.
The stock lost 200 cents to 130.50 rand by 1240 GMT in a volume of 183,900 shares.

De Beers said it would stop buying Russian stones under an old marketing agreement after December 31 and gave the Russian authorities until then to sign a new pact, which has been on hold since February.

The Russian news took the shine off record sales by the group's Central Selling Organisation (CSO) in 1996. The CSO, which accounts for some 75 percent of the global market, said 1996 sales rose seven percent to $4.834 billion.
"The shares are being sold on the back of the Russian news. There are a lot of small sellers," said one dealer.
"But there are also a lot of buying orders and the share should remain underpinned by the record sales. The fundamentals are good."
